headline: Longs lost $372M to liquidations in a day and funding turned negative; stablecoins shrank $6B in a week and Fear & Greed hit 20.
summary: Leverage has started to flush: $372M of longs liquidated in a day and funding went negative, but open interest is down only 3.6% and still in the 97th percentile. Short-term holder loss-taking widened and the close fell out of their −1σ cost band. Dollars are leaving through both stablecoins and ETFs; the plan hedges only after 5 closes below 73,036, and today is day 2.

overview.lead: Selling moved from spot into leverage today: longs were liquidated, funding flipped negative, short-term holders kept selling at a loss, and spot buyers have not shown up.
points: Close 68,236, −4.4%, on 2× the 20-day average volume; the intraday low was 67,500 and the close sat near the bottom of the day's range.
Long liquidations were $372M in a day and $793M over 7 days, close to 90% of all liquidations (Coinalyze).
Short-term holders realized 7,648 BTC of loss, more than 3× the 2,358 BTC of profit (CheckOnChain, Nov 13).
Stablecoins shrank $6B in 7 days; ETFs lost $51M on Nov 12, the 6th straight outflow session.

cycle.lead: The market stage is still bull, day 36, but the weekly bull–bear score turned negative for the first time, so the two cycle reads are starting to diverge.
points: The 200-day average at 73,036 is still rising (72,204 thirty days ago); the rule needs 30 straight closes below a falling average to revert to bear.

2 of 6 supporting lights are on: capital inflow (realized cap +0.03% over 30 days) and exchange supply (−0.29% over 90 days); 12-month momentum, MVRV vs its 1-year mean, short-term holder cost and STH cost vs true market mean are off.

The weekly bull–bear score went 0.32 → −0.03 and needs 4 straight weeks below zero to flip to bear; this is week 1. The Dawn Index tracks valuation instead: heat 34.8, still week 10 of Daybreak (Nov 12).
Tidemark bottom signal 30.8, outside its bottom zone; at the last 30 days' pace, a straight-line extrapolation puts the short-term holder cost crossing above the true market mean near Jan 23, 2027.

market.lead: This leg is down 21.2% from 86,594 over 53 days, already deeper than the median down leg of this cycle; the Sell Pressure Index is at 100 with momentum 0.12, the bottom combination.
points: The bottom combination has fired 20 times since 2012; 30 days later price was higher 11 times, median +1.8%, worse than any day's +3.2%, and after Aug 2014 and May 2022 price fell another 40%+.
Price sits at the 29th percentile of the past year, 7% above the q10 line at 63,547.

deriv.lead: Longs paid 10% funding for one day and then a batch was liquidated, yet open interest barely moved and estimated liquidations below the close are still 5× those above.
points: This page's finding: only part of the leverage is gone; open interest went 351,132 → 338,572 BTC and three-venue funding 10.3% → −0.9%.
Estimated long liquidation bands sit at 66.4–67.4K (2.1% below the close) and 63.8–66.3K (4.8% below), built from Coinalyze's aggregated open interest plus assumed leverage.
The 25-delta risk reversal is −4.5, puts priced above calls, so the market is buying downside protection; DVOL at 39.9 did not jump, and 7-day and 90-day implied vol are both 38–39%.
The largest ask wall is $214M at 68,000 and the largest bid wall $163M at 67,000, both on Hyperliquid perps.

flows.lead: The main exit for dollars has moved from ETFs to stablecoins: $6B redeemed in a week, 4× the ETF outflow over the same stretch.
points: This page's finding: stablecoins −2.04% in 7 days, 1.7th percentile of the past year; −$16.2B over 30 days (DefiLlama).
ETFs −$51M on Nov 12 (CoinMarketCap), the 6th straight outflow session; TradingNEWS reported −$284M for the same day without naming a source, too far apart to reconcile, so this site's figure stands.
Coinbase premium net of USDT averages −0.008% over 7 days, close to zero; USDT trades at $0.999 and its month-to-date average is the lowest in 4 years.
Polymarket puts a December hike at 96.3%; the 2-year yield is 4.88%, 0.88 points above the top of the Fed's range.

onchain.lead: Short-term holder capitulation is still widening and price has dropped out of their −1σ cost band, while long-term holder loss-taking is not keeping pace.
points: This page's finding: the close broke the −1σ short-term holder cost band at 68,416, where price has spent only 7.4% of days in 4 years; loss-taking intensity is 5.5, day 4 of concentrated loss-taking.
STH-SOPR 0.975, below 1 for 8 days and deeper than the Oct 30 low of 0.992 (CheckOnChain, Nov 13).

Long-term holders realized $1.5B of loss over 7 days versus $3.6B at the Jun 30 low; 38.2% of long-term holder supply is at a loss, and an estimated drop to 61,000 would push that past this cycle's peak.
7-day average hashrate 930 EH/s, −10.3% in a week; the Nov 14 difficulty adjustment is estimated at −8.8%.

exit.lead: The exit plan has not fired; this is day 2 below the 200-day average, 3 days short of the hedge condition.
points: Hedge rule: 5 straight closes below the 200-day average at 73,036 → cut 20%, earliest on the Nov 16 close; buy back after 5 straight closes above or when the MVRV Z 7-day average drops below 0.5, now 0.66.
MVRV ÷ prior-cycle peak is 0.477, far from the 0.75 line (112,082); the top-three indicators read 26/22/22, all low (Nov 12).

news.title: BTC fell as low as 67,922 intraday and crypto liquidations hit $1.47B in 24 hours, $1.31B of it longs
news.read: This site's Coinalyze data shows $372M of BTC long liquidations in a day and three-venue funding flipping from 10.3% to −0.9%, so the leverage added the day before was flushed. But open interest only fell from 351,132 to 338,572 BTC and is still in the 97th percentile since 2021; the cascade has started, not finished.

news.title: US October PPI rose 0.3% m/m, below the 0.4% forecast; the annual rate hit 6.5%, the highest since November 2022
news.read: The monthly print was a touch soft but the annual rate is still climbing, and Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said inflation has proved "far more persistent" than predicted. Polymarket still puts a December hike at 96.3%; for BTC this is a rising cost of money in the background, not a cycle call on its own.

news.title: The dollar held near a 19-month high and the 2-year yield rose about 32bp this week to 4.84%
news.read: This site reads the 2-year at 4.88%, 0.88 points above the top of the Fed's range, so bonds are pricing more than one hike. A strong dollar adds a reason to redeem stablecoins, in line with this week's −2.04% supply drop; the two happening together does not make one the cause of the other.

news.title: HSBC cut Nvidia to hold and its target from $375 to $170; Nvidia closed about 2% lower and the Nasdaq fell 0.90%
news.read: Tech is still digesting the CEO's exit: Nasdaq fell 0.9% while BTC fell 4.4%, the same shock amplified several times by leverage. The 30-day correlation is 0.68, and Nvidia's Nov 17 earnings are the next transmission point.

news.title: Spot BTC ETFs saw $284M of net outflows on Nov 12, a 6th straight day; IBIT lost $204M, its 10th straight session
news.read: Same direction as this site, very different size: CoinMarketCap shows only −$51M for that day, the article names no source, and no second independent source was found, so no provisional figure is added. Either way it is 6 straight outflow sessions, and US spot demand has not come back.

news.title: BTC fell about 8% below Strategy's average cost of $75,456; MSTR closed down 6.49% on Thursday
news.read: This site's CoinGecko data shows Strategy holding 850,363 BTC, −9.6% on paper. Trading below cost does not force selling, since its debt has no price-triggered margin call; the effect is that its share-funded buying may slow, which removes a steady buyer.

news.title: Glassnode: stablecoin supply shrank $14.2B in 30 days, the fastest since June 2022
news.read: On this site's DefiLlama basis, supply is −$16.2B over 30 days and −$6B over 7 days to Nov 13, so redemptions are accelerating. Stablecoins are the most direct buying power on exchanges, and when they shrink there is less money willing to catch a drop.

findings.title: Longs are being flushed, but open interest is down only 3.6%
findings.lean_why: Only a small part of the leverage is gone and estimated liquidations below are still 5× those above, so another drop could again be amplified by forced selling.
findings.what: Some of the leverage added yesterday was flushed today: $372M of longs liquidated in a day and three-venue funding went 10.3% → −0.9% (Coinalyze, exchanges, Nov 13). Yesterday funding was back at 10% within a day; today it went negative within a day, so the longs did not last two days.
findings.why: By venue, it is longs leaving: Hyperliquid funding went 11% → −6.6% and Binance 9.8% → 6.5%; perp takers sold 29,515 BTC more than they bought in the day. But total open interest only fell from 351,132 to 338,572 BTC, still in the 97th percentile since 2021, and 76.1% of Binance accounts are long, also 97th percentile, so retail longs have not left. On spot, Coinbase takers sold 6,196 BTC more than they bought over 7 days, 1st percentile in four years; US spot is not the one catching this.
findings.alt: Negative funding can also come from new shorts paying, not only longs leaving; Coinalyze's daily open interest and funding are closing snapshots that miss positions re-added after intraday liquidations. The liquidation record lacks Hyperliquid and Deribit, so totals run low; the liquidation bands are estimates on assumed leverage.
findings.history: Days with more than 72% of accounts long occurred 26 times in the past year; 90 days later price was higher only 10 times, median −7% (any day: 53% higher). A negative 7-day funding average has happened 13 times, with price higher 90 days later 10 times; the 7-day average is still 7.1% this time, nowhere near that.
findings.so: The cascade has begun but most of the fuel is still there: 25,325 BTC of estimated liquidations within 5% below the close versus 4,799 BTC above. This extends Nov 12's "leverage not flushed" read; the difference is that liquidations have started.
findings.next: Over the next week, watch open interest. A drop below 325K BTC would mean leverage has really left and refutes this; 7-day long liquidations above $1B would mean the cascade is widening, confirming it.

findings.title: Close fell out of the −1σ short-term holder cost band; loss-taking is double September's
findings.lean_why: Loss-taking is growing and short-term supply keeps coming out, but this position has usually shown up late in declines and returns afterward looked like any other day.
findings.what: Short-term holders are capitulating faster: the 68,236 close broke the −1σ band of their cost at 68,416, and the network-wide loss peak is 11.13bp, double the 5.41bp at the Sep 15 low (Bitview, Nov 13).
findings.why: Losses are doing the pushing: versus 7 days ago, short-term holder realized profit is −38.7% and realized loss +78.4%, with 7,648 BTC of loss more than 3× the profit (CheckOnChain). Loss-taking intensity is 5.5, day 4 of concentration, and this stretch peaked today; STH-SOPR is 0.975, below 1 for 8 days. Only 22.4% of short-term supply is in profit (Bitview), and relative unrealized profit is 35.2%, at the 35% floor for 9 days. Long-term holders have not accelerated: $1.5B of realized loss over 7 days versus $3.6B at the Jun 30 low; LTH-SOPR 0.946.
findings.alt: All of this is per-UTXO, so exchange wallet consolidation also counts as loss-taking; CheckOnChain figures are smoothed and lag about a day. A loss peak needs 7 days on either side to confirm, and another leg down would make today's 11.13 short of this stretch's top.
findings.history: Lower price with larger loss-taking has occurred 58 times since 2013; 30 days later price was higher 44 times, median +6.9%. Concentrated short-term holder loss-taking below the 200-day average happened 23 times, with price higher 30 days later 10 times, median −0.8%, about the same as any day under that condition. Price closed below −1σ on only 7.4% of days in the past 4 years.
findings.so: The sellers in this leg are still short-term holders, with long-term holders absent; the kind of joint short- and long-term capitulation seen at the end of June has not appeared. Nov 12's "loss-taking widens" is confirmed today.
findings.next: Two paths over the next week: short-term holder realized loss above 9,000 BTC would mean capitulation is widening further; a close back above the −0.5σ band at 73,312 would mean this wave of loss-taking is done, refuting this.

findings.title: Stablecoins redeemed $6B in a week, leaving faster than ETF money
findings.lean_why: Stablecoins that can buy BTC on exchanges are shrinking, so there is less money willing to catch a drop.
findings.what: The main exit for dollars has shifted to stablecoins: supply fell from $293.8B to $287.8B in 7 days, −2.04%, the 1.7th percentile of the past year (DefiLlama, Nov 13).
findings.why: Over 7 sessions to Nov 12, ETFs lost $1.47B (CoinMarketCap), so stablecoin redemptions were 4× that, and the ETF daily outflow has already shrunk to −$51M. USDT trades at $0.999 and its month-to-date average is the lowest in 4 years, a sign of USDT being swapped back into dollars; the Coinbase premium net of USDT averages −0.008% over 7 days, so the US–offshore gap itself is near zero. Outside data agrees: Glassnode reports a $14.2B 30-day drop, the fastest since June 2022. Fear & Greed fell to 20 the same day, into extreme fear.
findings.alt: Stablecoin supply covers every chain and use, so redemptions by DeFi, payments and market makers count too, not only crypto buyers leaving; DefiLlama and Glassnode use different bases and their numbers do not compare directly. ETF figures for Nov 12 vary widely (TradingNEWS reported −$284M), so actual ETF outflows may be larger than this site shows.
findings.history: A sharp 7-day stablecoin drop has occurred 14 times since 2020; the median 30-day return afterward was −0.4% versus +1.9% for any day. After the most recent cases, price was −1.1% 30 days after Jun 4 and −23% after Jan 26.
findings.so: Dollars are leaving through two exits at once, so spot buying will not return quickly; that explains why no spot buyer stepped in while leverage was flushed. The Nov 11 follow-up ("stablecoins below $287B") is only $0.8B from confirming.
findings.next: Over the next week, watch whether stablecoins stop falling: below $284B means redemptions continue, confirming this; a positive 7-day change means dollars are flowing back, refuting it.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Running on Empty
items.points: BTC near 74K, below short-term holder cost of 75.6K, with only about 35% of short-term supply in profit; true market mean 77.5K; two-thirds of short-term supply sits above price, and the only thick layer below is 62–66K. Stablecoins shrank $14.2B in 30 days; the largest long liquidation band is 59.5–62.6K; holding the June low at 58.5K keeps August's trend reversal intact.
items.meaning: This site's short-term supply in profit is down to 22.4%; the stablecoin shrinkage it describes has widened to $16.2B over 30 days on this site's data to Nov 13 (see 2026-11-13-3).

items.title: Bitcoin: Correction or Reset?
items.points: Via media coverage: short-term holder cost 75,717, with BTC below it for 4 days; reclaiming it plus 3 straight ETF inflow days would mark a correction, otherwise a reset; 11 of 14 past breaks were reclaimed within two weeks. Futures open interest 701.9K BTC, up 3.3% while price fell, funding about 11% annualized.
items.meaning: Original not read, so not used as evidence; by its framing, a close 10% below that cost with 6 straight ETF outflow days points closer to a reset.

items.points: BTC near 75K, lowest since August; futures open interest of $37B fell only 1.1%, long funding payments still high; ETFs out $1.6B in the week; conclusion: defensive, longs crowded.
